title: Anchor-stimulus validation orchestrator for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build an automated validation orchestrator that runs deterministic stimulus (anchor prompts) against quantized model builds (FP8/INT8), evaluates a compact set of signal metrics, and emits pass/fail gates for CI and canary rollouts.
background: We currently have several ad-hoc quant calibration checks (calibration harnesses and golden suites) but lack a small, fast CI-ready validation suite that 1) exercises high-signal failure modes for FP8/INT8, 2) produces interpretable metric deltas, and 3) plugs into rollout gates for Dedicated/Hosted deployments.
scope: Design and implement: 1) an anchor stimulus corpus (200 short prompts + 50 long-context edge cases), 2) deterministic inference runner with fixed sampling, 3) metric extraction pipeline, 4) rules engine for pass/fail, and 5) CI/canary integration (GitHub Actions + internal rollout service). Does NOT include replacement of full golden corpus or end-to-end UX for SRE dashboards (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Anchor corpus created and stored in /datasets/anchors/quant/ (200 short + 50 long), annotated with tags and expected semantics
Orchestrator can run against a model artifact id and return JSON with metrics within 60s for short-corpus and 300s for long-corpus
Rules engine evaluates metrics and returns PASS|FAIL using configurable thresholds stored per-release
Integration test demonstrates failure when running a deliberately degraded INT8 build and PASS for baseline float16 reference
Docs: runbook + README + example GitHub Action are merged and linked from the PR
steps: Assemble initial anchor corpus: stratified sampling across domains + adversarial perturbations
Implement deterministic runner: temperature=0, top_p=1.0, seed fixed, padding and kv-cache warmup for long-contexts
Wire metric extractors and small postprocessing scripts (embedding service, edit-distance, rouge)
Build rules engine with per-release threshold config and human-review override flag
Add GitHub Action job and example canary pipeline hook, smoke tests, and quick-local runner
Run smoke sweep across last 10 quantization CI artifacts and record deltas in a perf dashboard

notes: Trade-offs: smaller anchor set yields faster CI but higher Type II miss risk; chosen compromise is 250 prompts with stratified domain coverage
Runner will default to deterministic decoding; for stochastic models we will provide an optional sampling-run mode but it will be separate from CI gates
We will normalize comparisons vs a float16 baseline using the same tokenizer and prompt canonicalization to reduce spurious diffs
Plan to include per-layer sensitivity tags in follow-up triage artifacts for any failing anchors
